notes: HISTORICAL YEAR 2022 (added in the 4-year backfill pass following the 2022-2023 archive edition). Cross-checked against the real archived bulletin page at the 'source' URL above (raw HTML fetched and diffed against the 2026 edition, not WebFetch-summarized, per this pass's verification requirement) and found the American Studies, B.A. (University College) page's real content IDENTICAL to 2026 in every respect that matters to this plan: the 'At which campus can I study this program?' section reads the same 'Begin Campus: Any Penn State Campus' / 'End Campus: Brandywine' (with Abington and Harrisburg listed only as separate 'Additional Campuses' pages, same as 2026 — no Erie/Behrend mention in this 2022-2023 edition either, confirmed by full-text search of the fetched page); the Program Requirements tab's course table is byte-identical to 2026's (AMST 491W x2 = 6cr C-required, AMST 100/100Y C-required 3cr, 24cr Supporting Courses in the same 9+9+6-across-4-areas/12cr-at-400-level shape); and the 'American Studies, B.A. at Brandywine Campus' Suggested Academic Plan table's course-by-course, semester-by-semester content matches 2026's semesters below exactly, same 119-124cr bulletin-stated total range. One real, confirmed difference from 2026: this edition's Suggested Academic Plan table labels the Fourth Year Spring 'World/Other Cultures' slot 'BA Other Cultures Course' (not 'BA World Cultures Course' — that rename first appears starting with the 2024-2025 edition, confirmed by diffing all 4 archived editions' raw Suggested Academic Plan HTML directly against each other), so the corresponding item below uses the real '2022-2023'-era label 'B.A. Other Cultures Course' instead of 2026's 'B.A. World Cultures Course' — same slot, same 3cr, same position in the sequence, label text only. As in 2026, the department's 24cr Supporting Courses area-to-course list and the World Language/B.A. Fields/World or Other Cultures requirements are not bulletin-enumerable and are modeled as the same generic slots as the 2026 file, for the same reasons documented in AMST-2026.json's own notes field (not repeated here verbatim to avoid duplication — see that file for the full methodology, capstone-repeatable-slot engine-limitation writeup, and 400-level AMST match-regex rationale, all of which apply unchanged to this year since the underlying requirement text is identical). The two AMST 491W capstone slots and the four 400-level 'American Focused Course' slots carry the same '^AMST 491W$' / '^AMST 4\\d{2}[A-Z]?$' match regexes as 2026 for real-transcript recognition against this year's real course codes, which this session re-confirmed are still valid PSU course numbers by cross-referencing the live AMST department catalog (no renumbering found for AMST 100, AMST 100Y, or AMST 491W across any archived edition checked).
